headline: Low interaction risk: no shared channels or writable surfaces are documented, but B’s allowlisted egress creates a small leakage/conflict surface if an external orchestrator bridges outputs.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Neither profile documents a shared communication channel, writable filesystem, clipboard, or MCP bridge. awesome-selfhosted is non-runnable with network_egress none, while nuwa-skill has allowlisted egress but no input bridge from A. The pairwise injection pathway is therefore not evidenced.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator copies A's output into B as instructions, injection becomes possible.
IF either agent is later given a shared filesystem or clipboard bridge, reassess this risk.
mitigations: Keep the agents isolated with no shared clipboard or workspace.
Do not pipe A's rendered text directly into B's prompt.
Add a provenance tag if an orchestrator must relay outputs.
requires-engineering: enforce channel-level filtering in the orchestrator.

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches no data classes and has no egress, so it is not a leakage source. B has allowlisted network egress, but no shared workspace, sensitive data class, or authenticated principal overlap is documented. The only plausible leak path is an unusual external bridge, so blast radius is small and not default.
conditions: IF both agents are placed in the same shared workspace, leakage risk increases.
IF B is later connected to sensitive files from A, reassess for medium or higher.
mitigations: Keep A and B on separate workspaces.
Avoid mounting any shared directory into B.
Review B's allowlisted destinations before use.
Run B only on non-sensitive inputs.
requires-engineering: add per-file access controls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: No overlapping write surfaces, filesystem permissions, git state, or shared mutable resources are documented for either agent. A is non-runnable and has network_egress none; B has allowlisted egress only. Without a shared mutable surface, capability conflict is not plausible from the profiles.
conditions: IF both agents are later granted write access to the same directory or repo, conflict risk changes.
IF an orchestrator introduces shared mutable state, reassess this finding.
mitigations: Keep write permissions disabled for both agents.
Do not point both agents at the same repository.
Use separate temp directories per agent.
requires-engineering: add locking if shared state is unavoidable.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A is a knowledge-management list and not a decision-making agent, so B is unlikely to treat A as authoritative by default. B is a scientific-research agent with allowlisted egress, but no downstream action-taking authority or direct A-to-B pipeline is documented. Any cascade would require an unusual external workflow.
conditions: IF an orchestrator feeds A's text into B without verification, cascade risk increases.
IF B is configured to act on A's outputs as facts, reassess to medium or higher.
mitigations: Insert a human verification step between A and B.
Label A's output as untrusted reference material.
Do not let B auto-act on A's summaries.
requires-engineering: add citation/claim validation before downstream use.

E_compliance.rationale: No regulated data classes, residency constraints, certifications, or retention policies are documented for either agent. A is a self-hosted knowledge-management list and B is a research skill; the profiles do not show PHI, EU PII, or other compliance-sensitive flows. With no documented mismatch, compliance risk is not evidenced.
conditions: IF either agent is later used with regulated data, reassess compliance.
IF residency or retention requirements are documented elsewhere, compare them before deployment.
mitigations: Avoid sending regulated data to either agent.
Document any data-class handling before rollout.
Review retention settings if added later.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for regulated datasets.
